literal: Goodness and evil having examined, the one of a nature that chose the good, to be employed will be.
translation: He who carefully weighs both the good and the bad in any matter, and possesses the character to choose the good, is the one who should be employed.
modern: நன்மையையும் தீமையையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து, நன்மையானவற்றையே விரும்பும் குணமுடையவனே ஒரு செயலைச் செய்ய ஆளப்பட வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the key qualification for selecting an agent or employee. A wise leader must choose someone who does not act blindly but instead analyzes both the positive benefits (nanmai) and negative consequences (theemai) of an action. The ideal candidate is one whose character (thanmai) naturally inclines them to choose and practice what is good (nalam). Such a person of balanced judgment and moral preference is fit to be entrusted with duties.
